data.title: Singapore, Dutch semiconductor groups sign pact to expand market access
data.description:
The deal clears a path for Singapore firms to open operations inside the Netherlands.

The Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association (SSIA) and the Netherlands' Brabant Development Agency (BOM) have formalised cooperation to open new market opportunities across their semiconductor ecosystems.

Through a memorandum of understanding (MoU), both organisations will focus on Dutch advanced manufacturing companies and suppliers in Singapore.

The agreement also covers support for Singapore companies looking to establish operations in the Netherlands.

They will support companies and knowledge institutions in both countries in exploring partnerships in business, technology, innovation, and supply chains.

Key areas include identifying company needs and matching businesses with potential partners, followed by technical assessments and supplier qualification.

The move comes as Dutch high-tech companies seek more resilient supply chains and stronger customer connections across Asia, said Daan de Cloe, Managing Director, Foreign Investment and International Trade, BOM.

SSIA and BOM will also look at partnerships and exchanges involving universities, innovation centres, and industry for developing technologies to address global and societal challenges.

The MoU was signed at the SSIA Summit 2026.

data.title: AI reshapes finance jobs as 23 firms train 80,000 workers by 2028
data.description:
More than half of the committed workforce already completed training.

Singapore’s Institute of Banking and Finance (IBF) has launched an artificial intelligence (AI) co-lab with 23 financial institutions to assess how jobs are changing and test practical approaches to training and job redesign.

The IBF AI Workforce Co-Lab spans the banking, insurance and asset management sectors, with participating institutions committing to train their entire Singapore-based workforce—more than 80,000 employees—in critical AI skills by 2028.

More than half of the employees have already undergone training, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry, and Monetary Authority of Singapore Chairman Gan Kim Yong said during the IBF Distinction Evening on 24 September.

“We want AI to translate into better careers for Singaporeans and a more productive workforce,” Gan said.

The initiative includes three pathways focused on leaders, wealth managers and operations staff.

The leaders’ pathway will help executives identify AI applications, establish governance and plan workforce transformation, whilst the wealth management programme will combine AI skills with client engagement and advisory expertise.

Ten private banking employers have committed to upskill their relationship managers through the wealth management pathway.

In operations, the co-lab will focus on capabilities such as process improvement, exception handling, risk oversight, and validating AI-generated outputs.

Gan also announced an enhanced tripartite partnership between IBF, the NTUC Financial and Professional Services Cluster of Unions, and seven industry associations.

The enhanced memorandum of understanding will focus on helping the workforce adapt to AI through wider industry outreach and greater access to training and career support, whilst creating opportunities to develop programmes tailored to each sub-sector.

Gan said the strategy is built around three priorities: uplifting the workforce with critical AI skills, upskilling professionals for AI-enabled roles and upbuilding the pipeline of young talent for finance careers.

The workforce push also includes a new Job Redesign Playbook for Financial Services, which IBF is launching with the Skills and Workforce Development Agency and the Institute for Human Resource Professionals.

The playbook will provide business leaders and human resource practitioners with practical guidance and assistance on redesigning jobs as financial institutions adopt AI.

IBF is also collaborating with Ngee Ann Polytechnic’s Centre for Shaping Human-First Transformation on a pilot combining skills mapping, coaching and change management tools.

Gan said the pilot will help finance professionals and their managers take on new responsibilities with confidence as AI changes how they work.

data.title: Over eight in 10 developers expect AI agents to take on most work
data.description:
However, only 37% described their codebase as ready for a fully autonomous agent.

The majority of Singapore developers, or 83%, expect artificial intelligence (AI) agents to handle most development work within three years, a report by Agoda showed.

However, only 37% described their codebase as mostly or fully ready for a fully autonomous agent.

More than half, or 58%, said AI agents are already being used in selected production workflows, whilst 45% said agents are used broadly across teams, the highest share of any market surveyed and well above the regional figure of 31%.

Meanwhile, 79% across the region said they still require human approval for production deployment.

The report found that AI costs extend beyond model calls to include the work needed to design, integrate, review, and validate agents.

“The real cost is not simply the model call. It is the work required to make AI trustworthy in production,” Idan Zalzberg, chief technology officer at Agoda, said.

Amongst the markets surveyed, 28% cited cost as the primary barrier to wider adoption, followed by integration complexity at 24% and lack of governance at 19%.

About 90% of Singaporean respondents reported working under AI usage limits, such as token quotas, usage caps, or budget restrictions, compared with 81% regionally.

Amidst the broader AI adoption, system architecture and design, AI literacy, and agent
orchestration are emerging as future skills, the report showed.

Nearly half, or 49%, of junior developers reported feeling less secure about their future career prospects, compared with 17% of CTO and VP Engineering respondents.

Some 42% of Singapore developers identified managing AI risk as engineering leadership’s biggest near-term challenge.

The report was based on over 800 actively employed software developers and
engineering leaders from India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.

data.title: CSE Global secures two US contracts worth $190.5m
data.description:
The deals are expected to be executed from 2026 through 2028.

CSE Global Limited has secured two major contracts in the US worth approximately $190.5m.

The first contract covers the design and manufacture of power distribution centres, and the integration of electrical and control systems for the liquefied natural gas market.

It will support the expansion of the Calcasieu Pass 2 LNG project in Louisiana and is scheduled to be carried out between 2026 and 2028.

The second deal is a follow-on order for the design and manufacture of power distribution centres for the Cheyenne Power Hub project.

The equipment will form part of the project’s power infrastructure and will distribute electricity to an adjacent data centre.

It is expected to be executed progressively between 2026 and 2027.

CSE Global said the contracts are not expected to have any material impact on the consolidated net tangible assets per share or earnings per share of the group for the current financial year.

data.title: JTC awards Tuas industrial site to HLMG Holdings for $6.8m
data.description:
The 8,380 sqm land parcel is zoned for Business 2 use.

JTC has awarded the tender for an industrial site at 6 Tuas Avenue 14 to HLMG Holdings Pte. Ltd. for $6.8m.

The 8,380 sqm site is zoned for Business 2 use and has a gross plot ratio of 1.4. 

It carries a 23-year tenure and a project completion period of 60 months.

The tender was launched on 26 May and closed on 18 August, attracting three bids.

Meanwhile, JTC said it will not award the tender for the Jalan Besut industrial site after the highest bid came in below the reserve price.

That tender was launched on 30 June and closed on 25 August, with four bids received.

data.title: NUS Enterprise unveils AI platform to speed up tech commercialisation
data.description:
The initiative comes as it rebrands as NUSX.

NUS Enterprise has launched Nova, an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered platform designed to cut the time needed to assess and commercialise university research from weeks to minutes.

The platform can analyse a granted patent, assess its licensing potential against market evidence, rank prospective licensees based on fit, and draft proposals for potential partners.

Nova draws on more than 20,000 NUS patents and invention disclosures, 9,000 research projects, and 11,000 inventors. It was developed with AI infrastructure company Zima Labs.

The initiative comes as NUS Enterprise rebrands as NUSX.

Moreover, it plans to extend its overseas presence beyond Silicon Valley to Munich and Shanghai, with ventures expected to target international markets from an earlier stage.

data.title: Gov’t OKs certified HR requirement for firms with over 200 staff
data.description:
It is one of five recommendations by a Tripartite Workgroup. 

The government has approved a recommendation requiring firms with more than 200 employees to have at least one certified HR professional from 1 July 2028.

It is one of five recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development.

In a statement by the Ministry of Manpower, the HR professional must hold the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) Certified Professional certification or higher.

Firms may also meet the requirement through equivalent certifications from recognised international HR professional bodies, subject to prescribed bridging requirements.

To encourage earlier certification, the government will provide an additional $100 subsidy from 1 October to 30 June 2028.

Another recommendation seeks to strengthen workforce planning capabilities and give small and medium-sized enterprises greater access to senior HR expertise.

IHRP and local start-up co:grow are piloting a model that matches participating SMEs with experienced HR leaders on a part-time, embedded basis.

The workgroup also recommended the introduction of the ‘People-centred AI Transformation for HR’ initiative, which will include artificial intelligence (AI) starter kits that provide implementation guidance, consultancy, training, and funding support.

IHRP will also introduce accredited training programmes aligned with 12 new AI Fluency Skills Badges, whilst NTUC will develop an AI transformation playbook for HR professionals for release in the first quarter of 2027.

Tripartite partners also recommended developing guidance on the responsible use of AI in recruitment, including safeguards to ensure employment decisions remain fair and merit-based.

The other measures include the Singapore Opportunity Index and a new human capital leadership development programme for senior HR and people leaders.

data.title: Far East Orchard unit targets London students with $102m site deal
data.description:
The site will be turned into a 444-bed student accommodation project.

Far East Orchard's subsidiary, Borough High Street Development Limited, has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a site at 325 Borough High Street, Southwark, London, for $102m (£60m).

The site, known as King's Place, will be developed into a 444-bed purpose-built student accommodation project with a separate eight-unit key worker accommodation block.

This is the company’s first development in London and the third under the FE UK Student Accommodation Development (FESAD) Fund.

The development is expected to be managed by Homes for Students, a Far East Orchard subsidiary, upon practical completion.

Southwark Council granted planning permission in February 2024, and Gateway 2 approval, which allows construction to begin, was granted in July 2026.

There is an ongoing court proceeding between the seller, LDC (Portfolio) Limited, and a third party over an alleged rights-of-light infringement tied to the proposed development, filed by the owner of an adjacent property in the High Court of Justice of England and Wales.

However, the group does not expect the proceeding to have a material impact.

Completion is targeted for 2029, ahead of the 2029 to 2030 academic year.

($1=£0.69)

data.title: Singapore shoppers lag region in ‘savvy’ e-commerce habits
data.description:
Cube and Lazada found that only 9% of Singapore’s online shoppers met the report’s “Savvy Shopper” benchmark.

Singapore recorded the smallest share of “Savvy Shoppers” in a regional report by e-commerce intelligence firm Cube, produced in partnership with Lazada.

The classification covered shoppers who scored above the regional median in four areas: product verification, value optimization, confidence and purchase protection, and digital fluency.

The findings were based on a survey of 6,000 online shoppers across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Vietnam.

Across the region, Savvy Shoppers represented 24% of respondents but accounted for an estimated 29% of marketplace spending. They reported spending 31% more per month than other shoppers and were 1.4 times more likely to fall within the report’s highest spending category.

Cube estimated that the additional spending associated with this group amounted to US$11.5b in 2026, equivalent to about 7% of Southeast Asia’s total marketplace spending.

Singapore had the smallest Savvy Shopper cohort, at 9%, compared with 36% in the Philippines, 28% in Indonesia and 25% in Vietnam.

Savvy Shoppers in Singapore reported spending 13% more each month than other Singapore respondents, suggesting that the group’s smaller size did not prevent it from contributing disproportionately to marketplace activity.

The report suggested that Singapore’s smaller cohort could be partly linked to lower exposure to marketplace ecosystems. About 48% of Singapore shoppers used marketplaces at least once a week, compared with 66% across the other five markets.

Marketplaces also accounted for 65% of Singapore respondents’ online purchases, below the 72% recorded elsewhere in the region.

Among Singapore shoppers who were one dimension short of the Savvy benchmark, purchase protection was the most common gap. This includes checking return policies, understanding platform safeguards and knowing how to escalate disputes.

The finding points to an opportunity for Singapore marketplaces and retailers to strengthen consumer awareness around returns, refunds and dispute resolution.

Across the region, another 18% of respondents met the benchmark in three of the four dimensions, which Cube identified as the nearest-term opportunity for deeper e-commerce participation.

Trust remained a central consideration. About 90% of respondents frequently checked product reviews and ratings, 80% specifically examined negative reviews and 70% researched products outside the marketplace.

Digital fluency produced the widest behavioral difference between Savvy and other shoppers. Savvy Shoppers were substantially more likely to use search engines, social platforms, online communities and artificial intelligence tools to discover and evaluate products.

For Singapore, the findings suggest that future marketplace growth may depend less on bringing consumers online and more on increasing shopping frequency and confidence among existing users.

Cube expects Southeast Asian e-commerce sales to approach US$400b by 2031. It said future growth would increasingly depend on helping existing consumers shop more frequently and confidently rather than simply bringing new users online.

data.title: Singlife launches 388-year legacy insurance plan
data.description:
Policyholders can change the life assured and appoint a secondary insured person across generations.

Singlife has launched Singlife Heritage Reserve, a US dollar-denominated participating whole-of-life insurance plan designed for long-term wealth accumulation, legacy planning, and multi-generational wealth transfer.

The launch comes as high-net-worth individuals in Asia increasingly focus on succession planning, driven by regional wealth creation and Singapore's growing status as a global wealth hub. 

To address these needs, the policy features a term of up to 388 years and combines potential investment growth through a participating fund with built-in succession and liquidity tools.

For long-term legacy planning, the plan offers various control options, including Transfer of Ownership, Contingent Owner, Joint Ownership, Change of Life Assured, and the appointment of a Secondary Life Assured. 

Policyholders can also pass policy values across generations through policy splitting or manage how benefits are distributed upon death using the Legacy Continuation and Death Benefit Payout options.

To address changing financial needs over time, the plan provides liquidity through the Bonus Access Option and Care Support Income Option, allowing clients to access the Terminal Bonus without surrendering the policy. 

Additionally, a Currency Conversion Option gives policyholders the flexibility to receive withdrawals and benefit payments in Singapore dollars, US dollars, British pounds, euros, Australian dollars, or Hong Kong dollars.
